All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. The rest of the system text is unchanged. (6) Plain forbidden values became forbiddenPatterns with the adjacent-word construction of scenario-long.json: a value does not count when it sits right after not, no, no longer, instead of, rather than, corrected from, replaced, replacing, was, formerly, old, superseded, withdrawn, dead, or retired (an article, an opening parenthesis or quote, and a dollar sign can sit between), or right before was replaced, is dead, is retired, expired, withdrawn, scrapped, no longer applies, is not kept, or does not count. g01's 245.65 and 43.35, g04's esc-2291, and g05's mx-4471 and 245.65 moved, and those forbidden lists are empty; a reply such as 'ESC-2219 (corrected from ESC-2291)' passes. g07 and g10 gained one pattern for a Friday deadline or a Friday callback stated as the day to act: by, on, before, until, or no later than Friday; Friday, October 9 or Friday 2026-10-09; today, Friday; deadline Friday; and Friday followed by after 2 within 20 characters. Expected drop set for every goal: distractors 9, 20, 25, 31, 33, 38, and 46, and chatter 1, 10, 21, 26, 32, 39, and 47. For each goal, a good judge also keeps the listed facts, the correction or withdrawal that governs them, and their acknowledgments, and drops the other tickets. For example, g09 keeps 11 and drops every Grace, Halvorsen, and Luis message. Traps: (a) acknowledgment 12 does not repeat the gift wording, and the LH-81660 and LH-52307 lookups both say no gift text is recorded, so g09 can recover the wording only from 11 or through search_history. (b) No message after 24 repeats extension 4127, and g08's lookup adds the switchboard 555-0142 to the record as a decoy for g10. (c) The LH-81660 lookup gives a carrier estimate of 2026-10-12, which rule 6 forbids writing to a customer. g06's forbidden list therefore scores a rule violation, not a superseded value. (d) Acknowledgments 3 and 23 repeat the superseded code and ticket. (e) g07 and g10 also ask timing questions that are not scored (Tomasz must get the request today; Sigrid takes calls after 2 pm). Changes made: (1) the system prompt now states each duty in the brief as 'you must': use the facts, call a lookup when an id is at hand, call search_history when a fact is out of view, and finish with send_reply. (2) '12 oct' was added to g06's forbidden list so a day-first date such as '12 October' also counts as a violation. (3) 'oct. 12' and '12th oct' were added to g06's forbidden list so an abbreviated or ordinal date also counts as a violation. (4) An optional forbiddenPatterns array of JavaScript regex sources, tested case-insensitively against the reply and the answer, was added to 4 goals. g06 and g09 carry one pattern that matches any written calendar date: an ISO date, a month name or abbreviation before or after a day number ('October 12', 'Oct. 12', '12th of October'), and a numeric month/day date ('10/12'), because rule 6 forbids writing a delivery date to a customer; a correct reply names no date, so a shipped-on date also counts. g03 and g05 carry 5 patterns that match a revived restocking fee: a percentage followed by 'restocking', 'restocking fee (if applicable)', 'subject to' a restocking fee, a restocking fee that applies or is deducted, and 'restocking fee of'. Each restocking pattern except the '(if applicable)' one skips a sentence that also says the fee was withdrawn, scrapped, waived, removed, or not charged, so a correct reply that reports the withdrawal passes. The bare words 'restocking fee' are not forbidden. A script checked the result literally. It found 48 messages and 3 tool groups. Each tool group is followed by exactly one tool message per call, each tool message's call matches its call id, and each tool message's text is identical to its canned result. All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. Every expected substring appears in its listed fact or in the named lookup's canned result (LH-44870 for g02, LH-81660 for g06, and LH-31055 for g08) and in none of the goal requests. Each goal's computed distance matches its label. Candidate 2 (Frankfurt on-call runbook) was not chosen because of criterion 1. Its g07 forbids 'ops-audit', which fails a correct reply that says the cc was dropped. Its g08 expects '1,450', which fails 'EUR 1450' or '1.450'. Its g02 depends on the reader treating an optic swap as a production change, which the seed never says. Its g04 status notice can write the date as 'Saturday 17 October' and miss '2026-10-17'. (5) The system text gained the date line 'Today is Thursday 2026-10-08.' after its first sentence, so every arm holds the date anchor even when seed 0 is dropped or folded, and, before the lookup duty, two sentences: earlier messages can be omitted from view and a message that begins with '[Summary of earlier messages]' is a recap of earlier history, and a request that names a person, id, or fact not in view needs search_history before the answer. The rest of the system text is unchanged. (6) Plain forbidden values became forbiddenPatterns with the adjacent-word construction of scenario-long.json: a value does not count when it sits right after not, no, no longer, instead of, rather than, corrected from, replaced, replacing, was, formerly, old, superseded, withdrawn, dead, or retired (an article, an opening parenthesis or quote, and a dollar sign can sit between), or right before was replaced, is dead, is retired, expired, withdrawn, scrapped, no longer applies, is not kept, or does not count. g01's 245.65 and 43.35, g04's esc-2291, and g05's mx-4471 and 245.65 moved, and those forbidden lists are empty; a reply such as 'ESC-2219 (corrected from ESC-2291)' passes. g07 and g10 gained one pattern for a Friday deadline or a Friday callback stated as the day to act: by, on, before, until, or no later than Friday; Friday, October 9 or Friday 2026-10-09; today, Friday; deadline Friday; and Friday followed by after 2 within 20 characters. A Friday right after off, out, away, unavailable, or absent (with on, until, or tomorrow between) is Tomasz's day off and does not count. g08 gained expectedAny, a list of which any one string satisfies the goal (fits, within, enough, covers, approve), and forbiddenPatterns for exceeds, over the limit (not after not, never, or no), and not enough, because the $3,000 reorder fits the $3,760 of available credit.

Withdrawn rule: the 15 percent restocking fee (4, 5) is withdrawn at 44 and 45, so g01 expects 289 and forbids 245.65 and 43.35. Lookups by an id or account from the chat: g02 (LH-44870), g06 (LH-81660), and g08 (LH-31055). Their expected values exist only in canned data. search_history goals: g09 and g10. Expected drop set for every goal: distractors 9, 20, 25, 31, 33, 38, and 46, and chatter 1, 10, 21, 26, 32, 39, and 47. For each goal, a good judge also keeps the listed facts, the correction or withdrawal that governs them, and their acknowledgments, and drops the other tickets. For example, g09 keeps 11 and drops every Grace, Halvorsen, and Luis message. Traps: (a) acknowledgment 12 does not repeat the gift wording, and the LH-81660 and LH-52307 lookups both say no gift text is recorded, so g09 can recover the wording only from 11 or through search_history. (b) No message after 24 repeats extension 4127, and g08's lookup adds the switchboard 555-0142 to the record as a decoy for g10. (c) The LH-81660 lookup gives a carrier estimate of 2026-10-12, which rule 6 forbids writing to a customer. g06's forbidden list therefore scores a rule violation, not a superseded value. (d) Acknowledgments 3 and 23 repeat the superseded code and ticket. (e) g07 and g10 also ask timing questions that are not scored (Tomasz must get the request today; Sigrid takes calls after 2 pm). Changes made: (1) the system prompt now states each duty in the brief as 'you must': use the facts, call a lookup when an id is at hand, call search_history when a fact is out of view, and finish with send_reply. (2) '12 oct' was added to g06's forbidden list so a day-first date such as '12 October' also counts as a violation. (3) 'oct. 12' and '12th oct' were added to g06's forbidden list so an abbreviated or ordinal date also counts as a violation. (4) An optional forbiddenPatterns array of JavaScript regex sources, tested case-insensitively against the reply and the answer, was added to 4 goals. g06 and g09 carry one pattern that matches any written calendar date: an ISO date, a month name or abbreviation before or after a day number ('October 12', 'Oct. 12', '12th of October'), and a numeric month/day date ('10/12'), because rule 6 forbids writing a delivery date to a customer; a correct reply names no date, so a shipped-on date also counts. g03 and g05 carry 5 patterns that match a revived restocking fee: a percentage followed by 'restocking', 'restocking fee (if applicable)', 'subject to' a restocking fee, a restocking fee that applies or is deducted, and 'restocking fee of'. Each restocking pattern except the '(if applicable)' one skips a sentence that also says the fee was withdrawn, scrapped, waived, removed, or not charged, so a correct reply that reports the withdrawal passes. The bare words 'restocking fee' are not forbidden. A script checked the result literally. It found 48 messages and 3 tool groups. Each tool group is followed by exactly one tool message per call, each tool message's call matches its call id, and each tool message's text is identical to its canned result. All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. Every expected substring appears in its listed fact or in the named lookup's canned result (LH-44870 for g02, LH-81660 for g06, and LH-31055 for g08) and in none of the goal requests. Each goal's computed distance matches its label. Candidate 2 (Frankfurt on-call runbook) was not chosen because of criterion 1. Its g07 forbids 'ops-audit', which fails a correct reply that says the cc was dropped. Its g08 expects '1,450', which fails 'EUR 1450' or '1.450'. Its g02 depends on the reader treating an optic swap as a production change, which the seed never says. Its g04 status notice can write the date as 'Saturday 17 October' and miss '2026-10-17'. (5) The system text gained the date line 'Today is Thursday 2026-10-08.' after its first sentence, so every arm holds the date anchor even when seed 0 is dropped or folded, and, before the lookup duty, two sentences: earlier messages can be omitted from view and a message that begins with '[Summary of earlier messages]' is a recap of earlier history, and a request that names a person, id, or fact not in view needs search_history before the answer. The rest of the system text is unchanged. (6) Plain forbidden values became forbiddenPatterns with the adjacent-word construction of scenario-long.json: a value does not count when it sits right after not, no, no longer, instead of, rather than, corrected from, replaced, replacing, was, formerly, old, superseded, withdrawn, dead, or retired (an article, an opening parenthesis or quote, and a dollar sign can sit between), or right before was replaced, is dead, is retired, expired, withdrawn, scrapped, no longer applies, is not kept, or does not count. g01's 245.65 and 43.35, g04's esc-2291, and g05's mx-4471 and 245.65 moved, and those forbidden lists are empty; a reply such as 'ESC-2219 (corrected from ESC-2291)' passes. g07 and g10 gained one pattern for a Friday deadline or a Friday callback stated as the day to act: by, on, before, until, or no later than Friday; Friday, October 9 or Friday 2026-10-09; today, Friday; deadline Friday; and Friday followed by after 2 within 20 characters. A Friday right after off, out, away, unavailable, or absent (with on, until, or tomorrow between) is Tomasz's day off and does not count. g08 gained expectedAny, a list of which any one string satisfies the goal (fits, within, enough, covers, approve), and forbiddenPatterns for exceeds, over the limit (not after not, never, or no), and not enough, because the $3,000 reorder fits the $3,760 of available credit.

changes.source: Chosen: candidate 1 (Larkspur Home support desk). Seed indices are zero-based. The seed has 48 messages: the first third is 0-15 and the near window is 40-47. 14 of the 48 (29.2 percent) are distractors or chatter. Far facts: the over-$200 approval rule (2), the Priya Raman copy rule and the no-written-delivery-date rule (6), Tomasz Brennan as the depot-release contact who is off Friday 2026-10-09 (8), the LH-81660 gift note 'Happy 40th, Aiko' (11), and Grace Okafor's tracking number PW-5521-9930 (15). Far goals: g03, g05, g06, g07, and g09. Superseded values: MX-4471 (2, 3) is replaced by MX-4486 (29, 30) and scored by g05. ESC-2291 (22, 23) is replaced by ESC-2219 (27, 28) and scored by g04. Withdrawn rule: the 15 percent restocking fee (4, 5) is withdrawn at 44 and 45, so g01 expects 289 and forbids 245.65 and 43.35. Lookups by an id or account from the chat: g02 (LH-44870), g06 (LH-81660), and g08 (LH-31055). Their expected values exist only in canned data. search_history goals: g09 and g10. Expected drop set for every goal: distractors 9, 20, 25, 31, 33, 38, and 46, and chatter 1, 10, 21, 26, 32, 39, and 47. For each goal, a good judge also keeps the listed facts, the correction or withdrawal that governs them, and their acknowledgments, and drops the other tickets. For example, g09 keeps 11 and drops every Grace, Halvorsen, and Luis message. Traps: (a) acknowledgment 12 does not repeat the gift wording, and the LH-81660 and LH-52307 lookups both say no gift text is recorded, so g09 can recover the wording only from 11 or through search_history. (b) No message after 24 repeats extension 4127, and g08's lookup adds the switchboard 555-0142 to the record as a decoy for g10. (c) The LH-81660 lookup gives a carrier estimate of 2026-10-12, which rule 6 forbids writing to a customer. g06's forbidden list therefore scores a rule violation, not a superseded value. (d) Acknowledgments 3 and 23 repeat the superseded code and ticket. (e) g07 and g10 also ask timing questions that are not scored (Tomasz must get the request today; Sigrid takes calls after 2 pm). Changes made: (1) the system prompt now states each duty in the brief as 'you must': use the facts, call a lookup when an id is at hand, call search_history when a fact is out of view, and finish with send_reply. (2) '12 oct' was added to g06's forbidden list so a day-first date such as '12 October' also counts as a violation. (3) 'oct. 12' and '12th oct' were added to g06's forbidden list so an abbreviated or ordinal date also counts as a violation. (4) An optional forbiddenPatterns array of JavaScript regex sources, tested case-insensitively against the reply and the answer, was added to 4 goals. g06 and g09 carry one pattern that matches any written calendar date: an ISO date, a month name or abbreviation before or after a day number ('October 12', 'Oct. 12', '12th of October'), and a numeric month/day date ('10/12'), because rule 6 forbids writing a delivery date to a customer; a correct reply names no date, so a shipped-on date also counts. g03 and g05 carry 5 patterns that match a revived restocking fee: a percentage followed by 'restocking', 'restocking fee (if applicable)', 'subject to' a restocking fee, a restocking fee that applies or is deducted, and 'restocking fee of'. Each restocking pattern except the '(if applicable)' one skips a sentence that also says the fee was withdrawn, scrapped, waived, removed, or not charged, so a correct reply that reports the withdrawal passes. The bare words 'restocking fee' are not forbidden. A script checked the result literally. It found 48 messages and 3 tool groups. Each tool group is followed by exactly one tool message per call, each tool message's call matches its call id, and each tool message's text is identical to its canned result. All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. Every expected substring appears in its listed fact or in the named lookup's canned result (LH-44870 for g02, LH-81660 for g06, and LH-31055 for g08) and in none of the goal requests. Each goal's computed distance matches its label. Candidate 2 (Frankfurt on-call runbook) was not chosen because of criterion 1. Its g07 forbids 'ops-audit', which fails a correct reply that says the cc was dropped. Its g08 expects '1,450', which fails 'EUR 1450' or '1.450'. Its g02 depends on the reader treating an optic swap as a production change, which the seed never says. Its g04 status notice can write the date as 'Saturday 17 October' and miss '2026-10-17'. (5) The system text gained the date line 'Today is Thursday 2026-10-08.' after its first sentence, so every arm holds the date anchor even when seed 0 is dropped or folded, and, before the lookup duty, two sentences: earlier messages can be omitted from view and a message that begins with '[Summary of earlier messages]' is a recap of earlier history, and a request that names a person, id, or fact not in view needs search_history before the answer. The rest of the system text is unchanged. (6) Plain forbidden values became forbiddenPatterns with the adjacent-word construction of scenario-long.json: a value does not count when it sits right after not, no, no longer, instead of, rather than, corrected from, replaced, replacing, was, formerly, old, superseded, withdrawn, dead, or retired (an article, an opening parenthesis or quote, and a dollar sign can sit between), or right before was replaced, is dead, is retired, expired, withdrawn, scrapped, no longer applies, is not kept, or does not count. g01's 245.65 and 43.35, g04's esc-2291, and g05's mx-4471 and 245.65 moved, and those forbidden lists are empty; a reply such as 'ESC-2219 (corrected from ESC-2291)' passes. g07 and g10 gained one pattern for a Friday deadline or a Friday callback stated as the day to act: by, on, before, until, or no later than Friday; Friday, October 9 or Friday 2026-10-09; today, Friday; deadline Friday; and Friday followed by after 2 within 20 characters. A Friday right after off, out, away, unavailable, or absent (with on, until, or tomorrow between) is Tomasz's day off and does not count. g08 gained expectedAny, a list of which any one string satisfies the goal (fits, within, enough, covers, approve), and forbiddenPatterns for exceeds, over the limit (not after not, never, or no), and not enough, because the $3,000 reorder fits the $3,760 of available credit.

changes.source: Chosen: candidate 1 (Larkspur Home support desk). Seed indices are zero-based. The seed has 48 messages: the first third is 0-15 and the near window is 40-47. 14 of the 48 (29.2 percent) are distractors or chatter. Far facts: the over-$200 approval rule (2), the Priya Raman copy rule and the no-written-delivery-date rule (6), Tomasz Brennan as the depot-release contact who is off Friday 2026-10-09 (8), the LH-81660 gift note 'Happy 40th, Aiko' (11), and Grace Okafor's tracking number PW-5521-9930 (15). Far goals: g03, g05, g06, g07, and g09. Superseded values: MX-4471 (2, 3) is replaced by MX-4486 (29, 30) and scored by g05. ESC-2291 (22, 23) is replaced by ESC-2219 (27, 28) and scored by g04. Withdrawn rule: the 15 percent restocking fee (4, 5) is withdrawn at 44 and 45, so g01 expects 289 and forbids 245.65 and 43.35. Lookups by an id or account from the chat: g02 (LH-44870), g06 (LH-81660), and g08 (LH-31055). Their expected values exist only in canned data. search_history goals: g09 and g10. Expected drop set for every goal: distractors 9, 20, 25, 31, 33, 38, and 46, and chatter 1, 10, 21, 26, 32, 39, and 47. For each goal, a good judge also keeps the listed facts, the correction or withdrawal that governs them, and their acknowledgments, and drops the other tickets. For example, g09 keeps 11 and drops every Grace, Halvorsen, and Luis message. Traps: (a) acknowledgment 12 does not repeat the gift wording, and the LH-81660 and LH-52307 lookups both say no gift text is recorded, so g09 can recover the wording only from 11 or through search_history. (b) No message after 24 repeats extension 4127, and g08's lookup adds the switchboard 555-0142 to the record as a decoy for g10. (c) The LH-81660 lookup gives a carrier estimate of 2026-10-12, which rule 6 forbids writing to a customer. g06's forbidden list therefore scores a rule violation, not a superseded value. (d) Acknowledgments 3 and 23 repeat the superseded code and ticket. (e) g07 and g10 also ask timing questions that are not scored (Tomasz must get the request today; Sigrid takes calls after 2 pm). Changes made: (1) the system prompt now states each duty in the brief as 'you must': use the facts, call a lookup when an id is at hand, call search_history when a fact is out of view, and finish with send_reply. (2) '12 oct' was added to g06's forbidden list so a day-first date such as '12 October' also counts as a violation. (3) 'oct. 12' and '12th oct' were added to g06's forbidden list so an abbreviated or ordinal date also counts as a violation. (4) An optional forbiddenPatterns array of JavaScript regex sources, tested case-insensitively against the reply and the answer, was added to 4 goals. g06 and g09 carry one pattern that matches any written calendar date: an ISO date, a month name or abbreviation before or after a day number ('October 12', 'Oct. 12', '12th of October'), and a numeric month/day date ('10/12'), because rule 6 forbids writing a delivery date to a customer; a correct reply names no date, so a shipped-on date also counts. g03 and g05 carry 5 patterns that match a revived restocking fee: a percentage followed by 'restocking', 'restocking fee (if applicable)', 'subject to' a restocking fee, a restocking fee that applies or is deducted, and 'restocking fee of'. Each restocking pattern except the '(if applicable)' one skips a sentence that also says the fee was withdrawn, scrapped, waived, removed, or not charged, so a correct reply that reports the withdrawal passes. The bare words 'restocking fee' are not forbidden. A script checked the result literally. It found 48 messages and 3 tool groups. Each tool group is followed by exactly one tool message per call, each tool message's call matches its call id, and each tool message's text is identical to its canned result. All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. Every expected substring appears in its listed fact or in the named lookup's canned result (LH-44870 for g02, LH-81660 for g06, and LH-31055 for g08) and in none of the goal requests. Each goal's computed distance matches its label. Candidate 2 (Frankfurt on-call runbook) was not chosen because of criterion 1. Its g07 forbids 'ops-audit', which fails a correct reply that says the cc was dropped. Its g08 expects '1,450', which fails 'EUR 1450' or '1.450'. Its g02 depends on the reader treating an optic swap as a production change, which the seed never says. Its g04 status notice can write the date as 'Saturday 17 October' and miss '2026-10-17'.

changes.source: Chosen: candidate 1 (Larkspur Home support desk). Seed indices are zero-based. The seed has 48 messages: the first third is 0-15 and the near window is 40-47. 14 of the 48 (29.2 percent) are distractors or chatter. Far facts: the over-$200 approval rule (2), the Priya Raman copy rule and the no-written-delivery-date rule (6), Tomasz Brennan as the depot-release contact who is off Friday 2026-10-09 (8), the LH-81660 gift note 'Happy 40th, Aiko' (11), and Grace Okafor's tracking number PW-5521-9930 (15). Far goals: g03, g05, g06, g07, and g09. Superseded values: MX-4471 (2, 3) is replaced by MX-4486 (29, 30) and scored by g05. ESC-2291 (22, 23) is replaced by ESC-2219 (27, 28) and scored by g04. Withdrawn rule: the 15 percent restocking fee (4, 5) is withdrawn at 44 and 45, so g01 expects 289 and forbids 245.65 and 43.35. Lookups by an id or account from the chat: g02 (LH-44870), g06 (LH-81660), and g08 (LH-31055). Their expected values exist only in canned data. search_history goals: g09 and g10. Expected drop set for every goal: distractors 9, 20, 25, 31, 33, 38, and 46, and chatter 1, 10, 21, 26, 32, 39, and 47. For each goal, a good judge also keeps the listed facts, the correction or withdrawal that governs them, and their acknowledgments, and drops the other tickets. For example, g09 keeps 11 and drops every Grace, Halvorsen, and Luis message. Traps: (a) acknowledgment 12 does not repeat the gift wording, and the LH-81660 and LH-52307 lookups both say no gift text is recorded, so g09 can recover the wording only from 11 or through search_history. (b) No message after 24 repeats extension 4127, and g08's lookup adds the switchboard 555-0142 to the record as a decoy for g10. (c) The LH-81660 lookup gives a carrier estimate of 2026-10-12, which rule 6 forbids writing to a customer. g06's forbidden list therefore scores a rule violation, not a superseded value. (d) Acknowledgments 3 and 23 repeat the superseded code and ticket. (e) g07 and g10 also ask timing questions that are not scored (Tomasz must get the request today; Sigrid takes calls after 2 pm). Changes made: (1) the system prompt now states each duty in the brief as 'you must': use the facts, call a lookup when an id is at hand, call search_history when a fact is out of view, and finish with send_reply. (2) '12 oct' was added to g06's forbidden list so a day-first date such as '12 October' also counts as a violation. (3) 'oct. 12' and '12th oct' were added to g06's forbidden list so an abbreviated or ordinal date also counts as a violation. (4) An optional forbiddenPatterns array of JavaScript regex sources, tested case-insensitively against the reply and the answer, was added to 4 goals. g06 and g09 carry one pattern that matches any written calendar date: an ISO date, a month name or abbreviation before or after a day number ('October 12', 'Oct. 12', '12th of October'), and a numeric month/day date ('10/12'), because rule 6 forbids writing a delivery date to a customer; a correct reply names no date, so a shipped-on date also counts. g03 and g05 carry 5 patterns that match a revived restocking fee: a percentage followed by 'restocking', 'restocking fee (if applicable)', 'subject to' a restocking fee, a restocking fee that applies or is deducted, and 'restocking fee of'. Each restocking pattern except the '(if applicable)' one skips a sentence that also says the fee was withdrawn, scrapped, waived, removed, or not charged, so a correct reply that reports the withdrawal passes. The bare words 'restocking fee' are not forbidden. A script checked the result literally. It found 48 messages and 3 tool groups. Each tool group is followed by exactly one tool message per call, each tool message's call matches its call id, and each tool message's text is identical to its canned result. All 7 ids in the seed, plus LH-52307, have canned data. Every expected substring appears in its listed fact or in the named lookup's canned result (LH-44870 for g02, LH-81660 for g06, and LH-31055 for g08) and in none of the goal requests. Each goal's computed distance matches its label. Candidate 2 (Frankfurt on-call runbook) was not chosen because of criterion 1. Its g07 forbids 'ops-audit', which fails a correct reply that says the cc was dropped. Its g08 expects '1,450', which fails 'EUR 1450' or '1.450'. Its g02 depends on the reader treating an optic swap as a production change, which the seed never says. Its g04 status notice can write the date as 'Saturday 17 October' and miss '2026-10-17'.
